- **Writing (signs that record language)** [`writing_invention`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/writing_invention.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high
- **Alphabet and mass literacy** [`alphabet_writing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/alphabet_writing.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Arabic script now carries dots and vowel signs; Syriac, Hebrew and Pahlavi are written alongside. Many town men can read a little; secretaries, scholars and merchants read well. Mass literacy is no one's aim.
- **Codex book and finding aids** [`codex_book`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/codex_book.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Books are paper or parchment codices copied by professional stationers (warraqin) in the booksellers' market. Paper makes books cheaper every decade. Local: Suq al-Warraqin (booksellers' market), Baghdad; Baghdad paper makers.
- **Woodblock printing** [`woodblock_printing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/woodblock_printing.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Paper, soot ink and carved seals all exist; block-printed charms appear in Egypt only in the 10th century. Printing the Quran would offend those who see copying it as devotion. Elsewhere: Tang China, printed charms, sutras and calendars.
- **Movable-type printing press** [`printing_press`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/printing_press.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Joined Arabic letters change shape by position, so movable type needs hundreds of sorts. No screw press for paper, no type metal.
- **Reproducing images (woodcut, engraving, etching, lithography)** [`lithography_engraving`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lithography_engraving.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Seal cutters engrave stones and dies for coins; nobody prints images.
- **Relay post and public mail** [`postal_system`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/postal_system.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. The barid runs relay stations with mules and riders along the main roads; its masters in each province report on governors to the caliph. It is a state service, not public mail; private letters go with travellers and merchants. Local: the diwan al-barid.
- **Newspapers and periodicals** [`newspapers_periodicals`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/newspapers_periodicals.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. News travels by the caliph's letters, read out in the mosques at Friday prayer, and by the barid.
- **Scientific journal and peer review** [`scientific_journal`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scientific_journal.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Scholars answer each other in epistles (rasa'il) and dispute in the caliph's assemblies (majalis). Nothing periodic, and nobody reviews before copying. Local: al-Ma'mun's debating sessions.
- **Encyclopedias and dictionaries** [`encyclopedia_reference_works`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/encyclopedia_reference_works.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Al-Khalil's Kitab al-Ayn, the first Arabic dictionary (late 8th c.), orders words by sound; Sibawayh's grammar is the standard. Encyclopedias of the sciences come later.
- **Library catalogue and classification** [`library_catalogue`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/library_catalogue.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept high. The caliph's Khizanat al-Hikma has librarians and copyists; stationers keep lists of what they can copy. No union catalogue; Ibn al-Nadim's Fihrist is 150 years away. Local: Sahl ibn Harun, keeper of the Khizanat al-Hikma.
- **Pencil, steel pen and durable ink** [`pencil_steel_pen`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pencil_steel_pen.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Writing is done with cut reed pens (qalam), soot ink (midad) and iron-gall ink. Calligraphers argue about how to cut the nib; a pen with its own reservoir is a 10th-century novelty in Egypt.
- **Shorthand (stenography)** [`shorthand`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/shorthand.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Secretaries abbreviate in the diwans, and Byzantine notaries know Greek tachygraphy. Dictation is slowed by the reed pen.
- **Typewriter** [`typewriter`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/typewriter.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low
- **Copying documents (copying press, carbon paper, stencil duplicator)** [`copying_duplicating`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/copying_duplicating.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Every copy is written by hand; a large book takes a copyist weeks.
- **Braille (tactile writing for blind people)** [`braille_tactile_writing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/braille_tactile_writing.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Blind men are respected Quran reciters and scholars who learn by ear and memory.
- **Sign languages of deaf people** [`sign_languages`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sign_languages.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Jurists accept the intelligible gestures of a mute person for contracts, divorce and oaths; deaf people sign at home. There is no taught sign language.
- **Knowledge in the vernacular; translation movements** [`vernacular_translation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/vernacular_translation.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. This is the translation movement at its height. Greek works come into Arabic, often through Syriac, alongside Pahlavi and Sanskrit, paid for by the caliph, officials, physicians and private patrons. Local: al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf ibn Matar; Hunayn ibn Ishaq (young, learning Greek); Yuhanna ibn Masawayh; the Khizanat al-Hikma (Bayt al-Hikma).
- **Beacons, flag codes and heliograph** [`signal_beacons_flag_codes`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/signal_beacons_flag_codes.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Fire and smoke signals are used on the frontiers and coasts. Across the border, the Byzantines run a beacon chain from the Cilician frontier to Constantinople. Elsewhere: Byzantine beacon chain (later linked to Leo the Mathematician).
- **Optical telegraph (semaphore network)** [`optical_telegraph`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/optical_telegraph.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low
- **Standard time and time zones** [`standard_time_zones`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/standard_time_zones.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Time is local and set by the sun; the hours of prayer follow shadow length and sunset. Astronomers know noon differs with longitude.
